analyst_view.overall: Leaders Lazio (32 points from 12, unbeaten in the league, fewest goals conceded with 9, 3-0 against Lecce last time) visit 13th-placed Torino, who are winless in four with only 2 goals in that run and lost 1-0 at Napoli. Lazio are still without Tavares, Sutalo and Marusic, all counted by the numbers, while captain Zaccagni is back in full training and likely to start on the bench. Torino, now coached by Ignazio Abate, have lost Ismajli after surgery (counted by the numbers), and Belghali is a knee doubt that sources disagree on; the numbers no longer list him as out. Neither side plays in Europe this week; the referee is Daniele Chiffi, a low-card referee (3.1 a game) whom the numbers already count.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals, already lifting Lazio for their 17 goals in six and counting Ismajli and Tavares on the missing list. My earlier +3% was because the numbers had Belghali out while he was only a doubt; they no longer take him out, so that reason has gone. Torino have scored only 2 in four but have not kept a home clean sheet in 11 league games, and Lazio concede little, so the two pull against each other; I stay at about 2.7.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.0 corners, already lifting Lazio for their 33 corners in six. Tavares, an overlapping left-back who drives Lazio's crosses, stays out and Zaccagni is likely only on the bench, while Torino's 3-5-2 with Cacciamani and Aboukhlal or Patterson on the wings is unchanged. Nothing points clearly either way, so I stay at about 9.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.2 cards, already cut about 18% for referee Daniele Chiffi (3.1 cards a game) and about 9% for each side because both have been booked less than usual lately. This is not a derby and neither side has suspension worries, so I see nothing the numbers miss and stay at about 3.2.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.7 shots, already moving Lazio up (+8.5%) for their recent volume and Torino down (-6.4%). The injury news on both sides is mostly in defence (Ismajli, Marusic, Sutalo), Torino's front pair of Adams and Simeone is expected to start, and Lazio's front three is close to full strength, so I stay at about 24.7.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.4 shots on target, with Lazio's 32 on target in six already counted (+9%). Simeone has a strong scoring record against Lazio, but Torino have managed only 22 on target in six, and Lazio's Isaksen and Noslin carry their attack as in recent weeks; I stay at about 8.4.
